regimes.d000_sft_clean: Qwen2.5-0.5B fine-tuned on clean SFT data (0% contamination)
regimes.base_pretrained: NOT AVAILABLE - pretrained Qwen2.5-0.5B signals need separate computation

s1_embedding.interpretation: RL alignment consistently increases S1 across all benchmarks. Medium effect overall, large on MMLU.

s2_minkpp.interpretation: S2 Min-K%++ is remarkably stable. Mean shift <1% on average, direction inconsistent across benchmarks. Negligible aggregate effect.

s4_selfcritique.interpretation: S4 shifts meaningfully on MMLU (large d=0.84) and ARC (small d=0.43), but decreases on GSM8K (small d=-0.32). Benchmark-dependent.

auc_reference.note: AUC computed using contamination labels from d005/d100 SFT doses. These labels indicate which benchmark items were injected into SFT training data at those doses. For d000 and rl_aligned, these items were NOT in training, so AUC~0.5 is expected.

q1_does_rl_change_signal_distributions.answer: Yes, significantly for S1 and S4; negligibly for S2
q1_does_rl_change_signal_distributions.details: All KS tests significant at p<0.01. S1 embedding shifts +7.8% on average (medium effect d=0.45). S4 self-critique shifts +3.0% (small effect d=0.32). S2 Min-K%++ barely moves (+0.4%, negligible d=0.01).

q2_s4_survival_after_rl.details: S4 shows large distributional shift on MMLU (d=0.84) suggesting RL changes the self-critique signal substantially. On GSM8K, S4 actually tightens (decreases, d=-0.32). AUC with d005 labels: rl_aligned S4 reaches 0.544 on MMLU (highest among signals for rl_aligned), suggesting some discriminative power persists. But on GSM8K/ARC, S4 AUC drops to ~0.51.

q3_monotonic_shift_direction.answer: Only S1 is consistently monotonic (always increases)
q3_monotonic_shift_direction.details: S1 increases across all 3 benchmarks after RL. S2 is mixed (+GSM8K, -ARC, ~0 MMLU). S4 is mixed (+MMLU, +ARC, -GSM8K). The non-monotonicity of S4 is noteworthy: RL may improve self-critique ability (lowering S4 = better calibration) for math tasks while degrading it for knowledge tasks.

q4_variance_amplification.details: For all 3 signals across all benchmarks, rl_aligned has larger std than d000. Most dramatic: S1 on MMLU (std 0.072→0.138, 1.9x). S2 on GSM8K (std 0.089→0.181, 2.0x). This variance amplification complicates threshold-based detection.

key_findings.base_model_gap: Pretrained Qwen2.5-0.5B base signals do not exist. The analysis covers 2 of 3 planned regimes. Computing base signals would enable full base→SFT→RL trajectory analysis.

implications_for_paper.claim2_signal_survival: S2 Min-K%++ survives RL alignment almost perfectly (negligible shift). S1 and S4 shift significantly. This supports the multi-signal design: S2 provides stable baseline while S4 adds complementary information, especially for knowledge benchmarks (MMLU).
implications_for_paper.practical_impact: The variance amplification under RL means detection thresholds calibrated on SFT models may need adjustment for instruction-tuned models. A joint multi-signal approach (IRT calibration) could absorb this variance better than single-signal thresholds.
implications_for_paper.limitation: Without base model signals, we cannot distinguish 'SFT effect' from 'RL effect' cleanly. The d000→rl_aligned comparison conflates any SFT done during Instruct model training with the RL stage.
